issues.description: Attribute 'orders' of class SealSaloon: the problem statement/documentation requires a modifiable List<Meal> named 'orders', but the provided solution implementation declares 'private Meal[] orders;' and the template helper (ArrayHelpers) and other classes operate on arrays. This mismatch between List<Meal> (in the problem statement) and Meal[] (in the code) creates confusion about the expected data structure, whether students should use java.util.List or arrays, and whether they should use ArrayHelpers methods or List APIs.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the specification and code consistent. Two viable fixes (choose one to keep exercise coherent):

Option A (prefer minimal code changes): Update the problem statement to require an orders attribute of type Meal[] (or an array) and explicitly mention using the provided ArrayHelpers helper methods for modifying the orders array. Update any UML/text that references List<Meal> to show Meal[].

Option B (prefer API change): Change the template and solution to use java.util.List<Meal> (e.g., ArrayList<Meal>) for SealSaloon.orders, remove or adapt ArrayHelpers accordingly, and update examples and UML to reference List<Meal>. Ensure helper code and tests (if any) are updated to use List APIs so students are not left with array helpers that conflict with the required type.
